Mostly UHT 125 to 250 ml packs (stable while sealed). Some 1 L versions are fresh and need cooling.
Full-cream or instant powdered milk in tins or bags. UNRWA emergency parcels have included milk powder, and it is the main way to get milk without a fridge.
Sealed can, stable. Used in desserts and tea.
Unsweetened, sealed small cans. Stable until opened.
Thin drinking yoghurt (laban up, mkhid, ayran). Short life without cooling.
Dry jameed balls keep for months unrefrigerated. The liquid jameed sold in tubs is chilled and perishable once opened. Used for mansaf and yoghurt stews.

Mild salted white cheese, also desalted for knafeh. Short life without cooling unless kept in strong brine.
Vacuum-packed brined cheese that can be grilled or fried. Keeps a few days unrefrigerated while sealed.

Soft fresh cream cheese in tubs. Needs cooling.
Semi-hard sliced or block cheese. Keeps a few days at 20C when whole.
Mozzarella and pizza-topping cheese. Needs cooling.
Fresh curd cheese. Very short life without cooling.
Small tubs of sour cream (shamenet).
Small sealed tins of about 155 to 170 g. Stable until opened. Some are vegetable-fat imitations.
UHT cartons that keep while sealed.
UHT whipping cream for desserts. Stable while sealed.

Chilled pudding cups (chocolate, vanilla, caramel). Need cooling.
